title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Form of Each Document Type
content:
Within the `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` product line, Aurelia Hanse Line offers six document types. This page records three characteristics that describe the physical and legal form of each type: how many originals make up one set, whether it is negotiable as a document of title, and whether it may go out on a received-for-shipment basis.

## Definitions

- **Originals per set** is the number of original documents that one issued set puts into circulation. A sea waybill is never issued in originals, so its figure is zero; an electronic bill of lading exists as one single electronic record on the eBL platform, which counts as one original.
- **Negotiable** means that title to the goods passes from holder to holder by endorsement of the document itself.
- **Received-for-shipment issue permitted** means that the type may be issued as soon as the booking's containers have gated in at the terminal, without waiting for them to be loaded on board.

## Values by document type

| Document type | Originals per set | Negotiable | Received-for-shipment issue permitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Sea Waybill | 0 | No | No |
| AHL Electronic Bill of Lading | 1 | Yes | No |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | 3 | No | No |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | 3 | Yes | No |
| AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading | 3 | Yes | Yes |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | 3 | Yes | No |

## Reading the table

- Four types are issued as paper sets of three originals: the straight, negotiable, combined transport and switch bills.
- Only the AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading carries the received-for-shipment permission; every other type waits for the containers to be on board.
- The AHL Straight Bill of Lading is a paper set of three that is not negotiable, so its originals cannot be transferred by endorsement.

## Points of judgement

**Does an AHL Sea Waybill ever show originals in circulation?** No. Its per-set figure is zero, so an issued waybill puts no originals into circulation at all.

**How many originals does an AHL Electronic Bill of Lading represent?** One: the single electronic record held on the platform.

**Hypothetical illustration.** Suppose a documentation party holds an AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading whose containers have gated in but have not yet been loaded. Reading the last column, that type does not carry the received-for-shipment permission, so the gate-in alone does not satisfy this characteristic for it; the same facts on an AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading would.
